Mixture Density Network

An MLP that outputs a mixture of Gaussians — learning multi-modal conditional distributions p(y|x).

Training Loss (NLL) — MDN vs K=1 Baseline
MDN (K components) Single Gaussian (K=1)

How it works: The MLP maps x → (π, μ, σ) for K Gaussians.

Loss = −log Σk πk 𝒩(y | μk, σk²)

Adam optimizer. The inverse-sine dataset is multi-valued in y — K=1 cannot fit it.

Dataset: The inverse-sine dataset maps y→x via x = y + 0.3·sin(2πy) + noise, then swaps axes. For a given x, there are multiple valid y values — a standard regressor predicts a blurry average, but an MDN captures each branch as a separate mixture component. Multi-branch has three distinct linear clusters. Heteroscedastic has variance growing with |x|. The darker teal/blue heatmap shows higher predicted density; colored lines trace each component's mean, with opacity proportional to its mixing weight πk.
